claim_en: NO MORE DIVINATIONS, AS TIME AFTER TIME — SAMSON'S CLAUSE; THE FACE TO THE WILDERNESS; ISRAEL BY ITS TRIBES; THE SPIRIT OF GOD WAS UPON HIM — A SPIRIT OF PROPHECY IN THE TRANSLATION. 'Balaam saw that it was good in the eyes of the LORD to bless Israel, and he did not go, AS TIME AFTER TIME, to meet DIVINATIONS' (24:1) — 'as time after time' Samson's clause (Judg 16:20) among six; 'divinations' (nechashim) written and pointed exactly as 21:6's 'serpents' without the article — the diviner's art and the fiery serpents one word (computed on the points); 'he set his face toward the wilderness' (one seat); 'he lifted his eyes and saw Israel dwelling BY ITS TRIBES' (24:2, one seat) — chapter 2's camp seen from the height (the exam's Bava Batra 60a reads the tents' doors); 'and THE SPIRIT OF GOD WAS UPON HIM' (one seat in this form) — 'the spirit of God' in the Torah at the creation (prefixed, Gen 1:2), Joseph (41:38), Bezalel (Exod 31:3, 35:31) and Balaam; Saul's 'and the spirit of God was upon him too' (1 Sam 19:23) the run; ONKELOS 'a spirit of PROPHECY from before the LORD' (computed, cut).
middah: ink (the divination-serpent homograph, the clause's kin and the spirit-phrase's seats computed; the translation's prophecy cut)

claim_en: THE UTTERANCE OF BALAAM, THE UTTERANCE OF THE MAN — THE AKEDAH'S WORD, DAVID'S LAST WORDS' FORM; THE OPENED EYE; THE WORDS OF EL, THE VISION OF SHADDAI — ABRAHAM'S WORDS; FALLEN WITH UNCOVERED EYES. 'The UTTERANCE of Balaam SON OF Beor, and the utterance of THE MAN of the OPENED eye' (24:3) — the utterance-word (ne'um) in the Torah at the Akedah's oath (Gen 22:16), the decree (14:28) and Balaam's four verses alone; 'and the utterance of the man' at three seats: Balaam's two and DAVID'S LAST WORDS, 'the utterance of David son of Jesse, and the utterance of the man raised on high' (2 Sam 23:1); Agur's without the vav (Prov 30:1); 'his son' for 'son of' the archaic form; 'opened' (shetum) a word of four seats — the exam's Sanhedrin 105a reads it blind in one eye; Onkelos 'the man who SEES WELL' (computed, cut); 'who hears the words of EL, who sees the VISION of SHADDAI' (24:4) — 'vision' (machazeh) is Abraham's word at the covenant of the pieces (Gen 15:1) and the Prophets' once; SHADDAI the patriarchs' name (Gen 17:1 to 49:25; Exod 6:3 quoting them), Balaam's two the Torah's only other seats; 'FALLEN, and with UNCOVERED EYES' — 22:31's uncovering made his title; 24:16 repeats the verse adding one clause (computed); Onkelos 'lying down' (cut).
middah: ink (the utterance-word's seats and David's form, the vision-word and Shaddai's seats computed)

check.note: 'the vision' of Shaddai — Abraham's word at the covenant of the pieces

claim_en: HOW GOODLY ARE YOUR TENTS, JACOB — PSALM 84 ANSWERS; LIKE ALOES THE LORD PLANTED — THE TENTS' CONSONANTS; THE TRANSLATION MAKES THEM LAND AND NAMES THE EUPHRATES. 'How goodly are your TENTS, Jacob, your DWELLINGS, Israel' (24:5, one seat) — 'your dwellings' (mishkenotekha) at four seats, Psalm 84:2's 'how LOVELY are Your dwellings' the echo; the Talmud's Sanhedrin 105b reads the tents as the synagogues; ONKELOS 'how good is your LAND, Jacob, the house of your dwelling' — the tents made land (computed, cut); 'like streams stretched out, like gardens by the river, like ALOES the LORD planted, like cedars by the waters' (24:6) — 'aloes' (ahalim) are 24:5's 'tents' (ohalekha) with other points: one consonantal skin for the tents and the spice-trees, Jacob 'dwelling in tents' (Gen 25:27) and the aloes of Proverbs, the Psalm and the Song its kin (computed on the points); Onkelos 'an irrigated garden by THE EUPHRATES... SPICES the LORD planted' (cut).
middah: ink (the dwellings-word's seats, the tents-aloes skin by the points computed; the translation's land and river cut)

check.note: 'your dwellings' — Psalm 84:2's 'how lovely are Your dwellings'

claim_en: WATER FROM HIS BUCKETS; HIS SEED IN MANY WATERS — MERIBAH'S PHRASE; HIGHER THAN AGAG — SAUL'S KING, HAMAN'S NAME; THE TRANSLATION REWRITES THE VERSE AS A KING. 'Water flows from his BUCKETS, and his seed is in MANY WATERS' (24:7) — the bucket-word's two seats (Isaiah's 'a drop from a bucket', 40:15); 'many waters' in the Torah at two seats — MERIBAH's 'and much water came out' of the struck rock (20:11) and this (computed); 'and his king shall be higher than AGAG, and his kingdom exalted' — Agag the king Saul spared and Samuel hewed (1 Sam 15:8-33), and Haman the AGAGITE's name in Esther (3:1 and four more) (computed); ONKELOS: 'THE KING who rises from his sons shall grow great and rule over many peoples, and his king shall be stronger than Agag' — the buckets and the seed rewritten, cut from the shelf's bytes.
middah: ink (the bucket-word, Meribah's phrase and Agag's seats computed; the translation's king cut)

check.note: 'from his buckets' — Isaiah's drop, the Torah's one seat

claim_en: EL BRINGS HIM OUT — 23:22 WITH ONE LETTER CHANGED; BONES CRUSHED; HIS ARROWS — THE HALF'S CONSONANTS; THE CRUSH-VERB LEVI'S; HE CROUCHED, LAY DOWN LIKE A LION — JACOB'S BLESSING OF JUDAH VERBATIM BUT TWO WORDS; ISAAC'S BLESSING REVERSED. 'EL brings HIM out of Egypt, like the horns of the wild-ox' (24:8) — 23:22's verse with the plural 'them' made singular 'him' (computed on the tokens); 'he devours the nations his adversaries and CRUSHES their bones' — the bone-verb's one Torah seat as a verb (Issachar's 'strong-boned ass', Gen 49:14, the homograph); 'and his ARROWS pierce' — the consonants of 'his HALF', the parser silent, right; the pierce-verb of Levi's blessing, 'crush the loins of those who rise against him' (Deut 33:11), and of 24:17 (computed); Onkelos 'the children of Israel shall eat the WEALTH of the nations' (cut); 'HE CROUCHED, LAY DOWN LIKE A LION AND LIKE A LIONESS — WHO WILL ROUSE HIM' (24:9) — JACOB'S BLESSING OF JUDAH, 'he crouched, LAY (ravatz) like a lion (aryeh) and like a lioness — who will rouse him' (Gen 49:9): 'who will rouse him' the two seats alone in the Bible, two words exchanged (shakhav for ravatz, ari for aryeh) (computed on both verses); Onkelos 'THERE IS NO KINGDOM that can shake him' (cut); 'those who bless you are blessed, and those who curse you are cursed' — ISAAC'S BLESSING OF JACOB REVERSED: Gen 27:29 curses first; Abraham's Gen 12:3 blesses first with another curse-verb; the arar-root's last two of seven (computed).
middah: E10 (the repeated expression — Jacob's lion-blessing and Isaac's formula in Balaam's mouth; the deltas and the order computed)

check.note: 'who will rouse him' — Genesis 49:9's clause, its second seat

claim_en: BALAK'S ANGER — HE CLAPPED HIS HANDS; THESE THREE TIMES — THE OTHER TIMES-WORD; FLEE TO YOUR PLACE; THE HONOR PROMISED AT 22:17 REVOKED; HIS HOUSE FULL OF SILVER AND GOLD — THE SECOND, GOOD OR BAD FROM MY OWN HEART; THE FORMULA'S SIXTH. 'Balak's anger burned against Balaam, and he CLAPPED HIS HANDS' (24:10) — the portion's second anger; the clap-verb's one Torah seat (the mockers of Jerusalem 'clap their hands at you', Lam 2:15); 'to curse my enemies I called you, and behold, you have surely blessed, these THREE TIMES' — pe'amim, the festivals' other word (Exod 23:17, 34:23-24), the parser reads 3: the ass was struck 'three FEET', the blessings counted 'three STROKES' — two times-words in one portion (computed); 'flee to your place' (24:11, one seat); 'I said I would surely HONOR you — and behold, the LORD has HELD YOU BACK from honor' — 22:17's doubled promise revoked in its own words; the hold-back verb of 22:16 (computed); 'did I not speak also to your messengers' (24:12); 'if Balak gave me his house full of silver and gold, I cannot pass over the mouth of the LORD to do good or bad FROM MY OWN HEART' (24:13) — 22:18's clause, the deltas computed ('good or bad' for 'small or great', 'from my own heart' added, 'my God' dropped); 'what the LORD speaks, that I speak' — the formula's sixth and last.
middah: ink (the clap-verb's one seat, the two times-words, the honor promise's two seats and the deltas computed)

check.note: 'and he clapped' — the Torah's one clap

claim_en: COME, I WILL COUNSEL YOU — THE INK NAMES THE FRUIT AT 31:16, THE SIFREI'S ADJACENCY THE VERSE'S OWN BACK-REFERENCE; THE END OF DAYS — JACOB'S WORDS. 'And now, behold, I am going to my people; come, I WILL COUNSEL YOU what this people will do to your people IN THE END OF DAYS' (24:14) — 'I will counsel you' one seat; the counsel's fruit is named by the ink itself at 31:16: 'by THE WORD OF BALAAM... in the matter of Peor' — and 'in the matter of Peor' stands twice at 25:18 and once at 31:16: the Sifrei's juxtaposition of 24:14 to 25:1 (R. Akiva's adjacency rule, against Rebbi's 'as far apart as east from west' — piska 131:1) is the verse's own back-reference; Micah's 'what Balak COUNSELED and what Balaam answered' (6:5) (computed); 'in the END OF DAYS' — the Torah's four: JACOB's deathbed oracle (Gen 49:1 'what will befall you in the end of days'), Balaam's, Deuteronomy's two warnings (4:30, 31:29) — the Torah's two prophecies of the end open with the same clause (computed). Onkelos: 'I will counsel you WHAT YOU SHOULD DO, and I will SHOW you what this people will do' — the counsel split into the advice and the vision (cut from the shelf's bytes).
middah: E28 (from-the-preceding — the adjacency of 24:14's counsel to 25:1's daughters, the Sifrei's dispute on the channel itself; the ink's own back-reference at 31:16 computed)

claim_en: THE FOURTH PARABLE OPENS AS THE THIRD — AND KNOWS THE KNOWLEDGE OF THE MOST HIGH, MELCHIZEDEK'S NAME; A STAR FROM JACOB, A SCEPTER FROM ISRAEL — JUDAH'S SCEPTER; THE CORNERS OF MOAB — JEREMIAH FUSES TWO VERSES; THE SONS OF SHETH; THE TRANSLATION'S KING AND MESSIAH. 'The utterance of Balaam son of Beor, and the utterance of the man of the opened eye' (24:15) — 24:3 verbatim; 'who hears the words of El and KNOWS THE KNOWLEDGE OF THE MOST HIGH' (24:16) — the clause 24:4 lacks (the deltas computed: one word dropped, three added); 'the Most High' as God's title in the Torah at MELCHIZEDEK's four (Gen 14:18-22), Balaam's one and Deut 32:8 — the Torah's two gentile priests share the name (computed); 'I see it, but not now; I behold it, but not near: A STAR steps forth from Jacob, and A SCEPTER rises from Israel' (24:17, one seat each) — the scepter Judah's, 'the scepter shall not depart from Judah' (Gen 49:10 — whose 'lawgiver' sitting 6 found in the well's song); ONKELOS 'a KING shall arise from Jacob and the MESSIAH be anointed from Israel' — the translation's own messianic text (cut from the shelf's bytes); the exam's Yerushalmi Taanit 4:5 has R. Akiva read bar Kokhba here; 'and crushes the CORNERS OF MOAB and breaks down all the sons of SHETH' (one seat) — JEREMIAH 48:45 FUSES THIS VERSE WITH 21:28: 'a fire went out from Heshbon... and devoured the CORNER OF MOAB and the CROWN of the sons of tumult' — the parable-tellers' fire and Balaam's corner in one prophetic verse; Sheth is Adam's son (Gen 4:25, 5:3-8), his sons all mankind (Onkelos 'rule over all the sons of man'); the crush-verb Levi's (Deut 33:11) (computed on the three verses).
middah: ink (the Most High's seats, Judah's scepter, Jeremiah's fusion and Sheth's seats computed; the translation's Messiah cut)

check.note: 'and breaks down' the sons of Sheth — Jeremiah's 'crown of the sons of tumult'

claim_en: EDOM AND SEIR A POSSESSION; ISRAEL DOES VALIANTLY; ONE FROM JACOB SHALL RULE — THE CREATION'S VERB; THE SURVIVOR — OG'S WORD; AMALEK THE FIRST OF NATIONS — THE FIRST OF ISRAEL'S WARS IN THE TRANSLATION; THE KENITE'S NEST IN THE SELA — MERIBAH'S ROCK-WORD, SITTING 6'S CROWN CLOSED; KAYIN — CAIN'S NAME; ASSHUR. 'Edom shall be a possession, and Seir a possession of his enemies, and Israel DOES VALIANTLY' (24:18, one seat; Psalm 118:15-16's clause) — Edom the refuser of 20:14-21; Onkelos 'prospers in possessions' (cut); 'one from Jacob shall RULE and destroy the SURVIVOR from the city' (24:19) — the rule-verb (radah) of the creation's 'let them RULE' (Gen 1:26) and the king's 'may he rule from sea to sea' (Ps 72:8), Onkelos reading it 'descend'; the survivor-word of Og's 'until no survivor was left' (21:35), Joshua's refrain (computed on the points, cut); 'he saw Amalek: Amalek was THE FIRST OF NATIONS, and his end is destruction' (24:20) — the first to fight (Exod 17:8), Amalek's sixteen Torah seats; ONKELOS 'the first of ISRAEL'S WARS' — Exodus 17:8 written into the translation (cut); 'he saw the Kenite: firm is your dwelling, and your NEST set in the SELA' (24:21, one seat) — the rock-word Moses was told to SPEAK to at Meribah (20:8, 10, 11), the Torah's five seats with Deut 32:13 — sitting 6's crown closed at its fifth; the Kenite Moses' father-in-law's people (Judg 1:16), Heber 'separated from KAYIN' (4:11); Onkelos renames the tribe 'the Shalmaite' (cut); 'if KAYIN shall be for wasting, how long until ASSHUR takes you captive' (24:22) — Cain's name in the pausal form; Asshur's Torah seats Genesis's four and Balaam's two (computed).
middah: ink (the rule-verb by the points, the survivor's and the sela's seats, Kayin's and Asshur's computed; the translation's readings cut)

check.note: 'your dwelling' — the Kenite's, firm, its nest in the sela

claim_en: WHO SHALL LIVE WHEN EL DOES THIS; SHIPS FROM KITTIM — DANIEL QUOTES BALAAM; ASSHUR AND EBER AFFLICTED; THE TRANSLATION NAMES ROME AND THE EUPHRATES; BALAAM RETURNED, BALAK WENT HIS WAY — JACOB'S CLAUSE; THE RETELLINGS. 'Alas, who shall live when EL appoints this' (24:23) — the seventh parable, 'who shall live' one seat, El's eighth and last; Onkelos 'woe to the guilty who live' (cut); 'SHIPS from the hand of KITTIM' (24:24) — 'ships' (tzim) one seat in this form; Kittim Javan's son (Gen 10:4), Isaiah 23's and Ezekiel 27's coast, and DANIEL 11:30 'ships of Kittim shall come against him' — the seer's clause quoted in the last prophecy; 'they afflict Asshur and afflict EBER' — the Hebrews' eponym, 'the father of all the sons of Eber' (Gen 10:21), the same pointing; 'he too is to destruction' — Amalek's clause (24:20, 24) (computed); ONKELOS: 'legions shall be gathered FROM THE ROMANS... and subjugate BEYOND THE EUPHRATES' — Rome and the river's far side in the translation's text (cut from the shelf's bytes); 'Balaam rose and went and returned to his place, and Balak too went his way' (24:25) — 'went his way' JACOB's clause when the angels met him (Gen 32:2), the phrase's two Torah seats; Balaam found among Midian and killed by the sword (31:8); THE RETELLINGS: 'the LORD turned the curse into a blessing' (Deut 23:6, Neh 13:2), 'I would not listen to Balaam' (Josh 24:10), Jephthah's 'are you better than Balak son of Zippor?' (Judg 11:25), Micah's 'what Balak counseled and what Balaam answered — from Shittim to Gilgal' (6:5) (computed).
middah: ink (Kittim's and Eber's seats, Daniel's quotation, Jacob's clause and the retellings computed; the translation's Rome cut)
